newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to sell 10pct Banco de Venezuela locally.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to sell 10pct Banco de Venezuela locally.

text.p: The Venezuelan government plans to place 10 percent of state bank Banco de Venezuela on local capital markets in a new auction slated for later this year, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
"We have asked that in the case of Banco de Venezuela that about 10 percent be placed on the local stock market," Matos told a news conference.

Spain's Banco Santander SA, Peru's Banco de Credito, Colombia's Banco Bogota and Germany's Dresdner Bank AG had shown interest in the bank but only the first two placed a deposit needed to make a bid. State Deposits Guarantee Fund (FOGADE) postponed a planned outright sale of the bank two weeks ago after political parties raised questions about the auction.
FOGADE President Esther de Margulis subsequently announced that the government planned to convene a new auction for the bank for the fourth quarter of the year.
Banco de Venezuela, the country's oldest bank, was the third largest commercial bank at the end of July with 418 billion bolivars worth ($880 million) of deposits.

FOGADE took over the bank in August 1994, when it fell victim to the country's massive 1994-5 financial sector crisis, which affected over half the commercial banking sector and cost the state over $10 billion.
